notes: Tab Item is a subcomponent: in Figma it lives in Coin Subcomponents and reaches designs through the Tabs slot, so every rule assumes it sits in a Tabs row. Evidence spans 5 October (0.1.78-3795b4c), 8 October (0.1.78-636f3f5) and 13 October (0.1.78-c1fa197, the installed build); the 5 October 'Package' and 'DOM' lines (no testID, no badge, tabindex=0 on every tab, no aria-selected) are superseded by the later checks. Examples pass modes on Tabs only: the Tabs facts say it forwards them to TabItem children, and the evidence says the item's own modes win. The truncateLabel prop is set by Tabs on a non-scrollable row (package doc); the guide does not mention it, so no rule covers it. Guide problems: Configuration says a Tab Item has no 'style options', but the package declares style and labelStyle override props (the guide presumably means design options; not changed here). Sizing's title says 'Tabs sets the width' while its description says a Tab Item 'is as wide as its label' (in a row that doesn't fit, Tabs shrinks it, per the Tabs evidence). The guide's copy does not mention #272 (with no active tab, or a lone idle Tab Item, the keyboard can't reach it), which the evidence records; the Tabs guide's Sources note does. The Dark mode gap (#197) was last recorded on 5 October.

useWhen.text: Use a Tab Item inside Tabs for each view: a short label that turns black with a gold underline while its view is showing.

from.quote: Use a Tab Item inside Tabs for each view: a short label that turns black with a gold underline while its view is showing.

avoidWhen.text: On its own, outside Tabs: a lone Tab Item stretches across its container with no row around it. Use it inside Tabs.

avoidWhen.text: The tab would do something, such as “Download”: it sounds like a button, but tabs only switch views.

from.quote: “Download” sounds like a button, but tabs only switch views.

absolute.reason: "only" describes what tabs do (switch views), the reason an action label misleads; it is not a separate constraint.

avoidWhen.text: The tab needs a disabled state: there is none.

from.quote: There is no disabled state.

from.quote: Names the view in a word or two.

placementAdvice.text: Always place a Tab Item inside Tabs.

from.quote: One view, one short label, and always inside Tabs.

absolute.reason: the principle has no condition, and the guide's Sources title ("Use Tab Item through Tabs") and Don't ("Place one on its own") agree: a Tab Item is a subcomponent that reaches designs through the Tabs slot.

placementAdvice.text: Tabs places the tabs 16 px apart; a Tab Item is as wide as its label.

from.quote: It is as wide as its label; Tabs places the tabs 16 px apart.

configuration.text: Set active on the tab whose view is showing: the screen marks it, and a Tab Item never selects itself.

from.quote: The screen marks the tab whose view is showing as active; a Tab Item never selects itself.

absolute.reason: "never" describes what the component does (it does not select itself), which is why the screen sets active; it is not a constraint on the designer.

configuration.text: Mark one tab active: one underline shows the current view.

from.quote: One underline shows the current view.

configuration.text: Do not mark two tabs active: only the first is underlined, which may not be the view that’s showing.

from.quote: Only the first is underlined, which may not be the view that’s showing.

absolute.reason: "Only" describes what the component renders when two tabs are active, not a constraint.

  <TabItem label="AY26" accessibilityLabel="Assessment year 2026" onPress={() => {}} />
</Tabs>
